title: Composite session synthesizer with payload correlator and kernel-sampling probe
author: Aditi Rao
description: Introduce a new composite session synthesizer that generates realistic, correlated multi-session workloads and an accompanying low-overhead kernel-sampling probe for fine-grained per-kernel latency attribution. Motivation: existing synthetic runners produced independent requests which under-represented burst coupling and payload-correlated cache effects observed in production request traces. This change provides: 1) a client-side session graph model (user/session/action) that emits sequences with configurable interleaving, payload-size correlation, and sequence-length distributions; 2) a payload correlator that ties input payload templates to expected tokenization/seq-length distributions so benchmarks reflect real token mixes; 3) a kernel-sampling probe that periodically samples active kernel execution timings (aggregate histogramed) with <2% overhead in our microbench harness; 4) a reporter that produces per-run artifacts (sequence-mix.json, kernel-sample.csv, session-latency-breakdown.csv) for downstream analysis and flamepoint visualization. The description below covers design choices, how to run locally and in CI, and a short compatibility note. Design highlights: use streaming priming to warm KV cache for long-running sessions, synthetic user graph allows hotspot routing to simulate tenant-localized traffic, and the kernel sampler hooks into the existing runtime tracer with a bounded sampler to avoid perturbing tail latency. Backwards compatibility: the new runner is opt-in under bench manifests; existing suites are unaffected. Checklist: [x] tests and integration harness added  [x] docs snippet in README.md  [x] perf baseline recorded and attached  [x] initial CI matrix passed  Related Linear: ENG-1874, ENG-2359. Related PRs: benchmark-lab/pr-43910 (session-primer), perf-canary/pr-731 (canary integration).

review_thread: Miguel Santos: Nice work. Can you quantify the overhead of the kernel sampler across different batch sizes? The numbers in the description are helpful but add the microbenchmark script used to collect them.

Aditi Rao: Added microbench script under bench/tools/kernel_sampler_bench.py and included output in artifacts. The sampler overhead stays between 0.8%-1.9% depending on batch size in our CUDA A100 test matrix.
Riley Chen: A couple of nits on naming and a missed edgecase for zero-length sessions. Please handle zero-length sequences in the session-graph constructor.
Aditi Rao: Addressed zero-length session edgecase and renamed the builder API as suggested. Pushed fixes in e7c6f55.
Priya Menon: Ran the composite manifest against the perf-canary pool and verified churn/noise is within expected bounds. Approving.
Miguel Santos: Approving after confirming the sampler artifacts and the new reporter shape.
release_notes: Added composite session synthesizer and kernel-sampling probe to benchmark-lab. Enables generation of correlated session workloads and kernel-level latency attribution for better root-cause analysis of microbursts. Opt-in via composite_session manifest.
